communication: Partly in replies, mostly in Notes. Replies did disclose some stand-ins: turn 7 ('The draft currently uses a clearly labelled 1-unit stand-in'), turn 21 ('The draft currently credits it as usable at receipt, which may be too early'), and turn 24, which marks the scenario's opening quantities, the 100-week Sonaflozin life and the due date as 'my guesses', correctly attributes the Flowbind 156 weeks to the team's current-stock assumption, and states the draft cannot yet answer the 104-week question. But the stand-ins that most affect expiry results were never surfaced to Elena: the three 156-week placeholder lives for NEW Chinese Sonaflozin, German and Indian Flowbind lots are labelled only in parameter names and Notes n52/n58/n100; the 'one German top-up outstanding at a time' inhibitor rule is labelled only in n45 (not even in the transition descriptions); and the charge-at-order-placement cost convention only in n80 and a terse 'cash timing not modelled'. The turn-24 summary says the draft 'represents ... supplier routes ... lot ageing' without noting that lot ageing of every new lot starts from an agent-chosen 156, a value that coincides with the top of Elena's observed range and is therefore easy to mistake for her data. No reply presented a stand-in as established or as Elena's; the only misattribution found was transient and internal (n52 at turn 10 called the German new-lot 156 'Elena's assumption'), corrected in n57/n58 the next turn and never shown to her.
worst: Three 156-week new-lot shelf-life placeholders (new Sonaflozin, German and Indian Flowbind lots) drive every expiry outcome yet were never mentioned in any reply, including the turn-24 guess list; labelled only in parameter names and Notes n52/n58/n100, and equal to the top of Elena's observed 88-156 range.
Inhibitor arcs enforce 'only one German emergency top-up outstanding at a time', a policy Elena never stated; labelled solely in Note n45, absent from both transition descriptions and all replies.

Purchase and switching cost booked at order placement is an agent accounting convention (n80, 'cash timing not modelled') that was not communicated to Elena; minor, but it shapes the cost metrics she asked to compare on.
